passage: Teacher's note. Kashish had lost her pencil box for the third time this term. This time I asked her not to look for it first, but to ask 'why' out loud. 'Why do I lose it?' 'I leave it at school.' 'Why do I leave it?' 'I rush at the bell.' 'Why do I rush?' Kashish thought for a while. 'Because I only start packing when the bell rings, and Chinmay is already waiting at the door.' She grinned. 'So I should pack before the bell.' The next day Kashish began packing five minutes early. By Friday the box came home every day.

qa.a: Kashish had lost the pencil box for the third time this term.
Kashish's grin suggested she was pleased, since she had found the cause and a plan of her own.

qa.q: What other step could help Kashish remember the box?
qa.a: Kashish could keep a small picture card in her bag listing what to pack, since a card reminds her even on rushed days.

qa.q: How might Chinmay have seen Kashish packing early?
qa.a: Chinmay was probably glad to leave without waiting at the door, since Kashish was ready when the bell rang.

grounding: Shows a girl who keeps losing her pencil box asking why again and again until she finds the deeper cause and packs before the bell.

subtype: Approach: keeps asking why until a deeper cause appears [Thinking]
passage:
Thursday
I lost my pencil box AGAIN. Third time this month. Mamma was upset, and Vijay my little brother laughed.
Tonight Mamma said, "Don't just say sorry, Maria beti. Ask why."
So I asked. Why did I lose it? Because I left it at school. Why did I leave it? Because I was rushing when the bell rang. Why was I rushing? Because I only start packing AFTER the bell, and everyone is already running out.
So it's not that I'm careless. It's that I pack too late!
Tomorrow I'll start packing five minutes before the bell, when Miss says "last question". I wrote it on my hand so I don't forget.
Maria 🙂

qa.q: How many times did Maria lose the pencil box this month?
How did Maria feel after working out the reason?
qa.a: Maria felt relieved and hopeful, realising she wasn't just careless but was packing too late.

qa.q: What else could Maria try if she still forgets?
qa.a: She could ask a friend to remind her at "last question", or keep a small checklist in her bag, so the new habit has a backup.

qa.q: How might Mamma see Maria's new plan?
qa.a: Mamma may feel pleased and proud that Maria looked for the real reason instead of just saying sorry.

grounding: It shows a girl asking why she keeps losing her pencil box until she finds she packs after the bell, so she starts packing five minutes earlier.

passage:
Sarita's slate pencil box had gone missing from the village school for the second time that week. Walking home past the mustard fields, her grandfather Deepak Dada asked, "Why did it get lost?"
"I left it on the bench."
"Why?"
"I forgot it."
"Why did you forget?"
Sarita kicked a pebble. "Because the bell rang and everyone ran for the bus, so I ran too."
"And why was it still out when the bell rang?"
She stopped walking. "Because I only pack after the bell."
Dada smiled and waited.
"So if I pack before the bell," she said slowly, "I won't have to rush."
The next day, when Masterji said, "Five minutes left," Sarita put her slate, pencils and box into her cloth bag. When the bell rang, she walked out with everything.

qa.q: What did Masterji say when Sarita started packing?
How was Sarita feeling when she kicked a pebble?
qa.a: She was frustrated and a bit embarrassed about losing her box again and being asked why.

qa.q: Which approach did Dada use, and why did it work better than telling her the answer?
qa.a: He kept asking why, so Sarita found the deeper cause herself and was more likely to remember the fix.

qa.q: How might Deepak Dada see Sarita walking out with everything the next day?
qa.a: He would feel proud and pleased that his granddaughter found her own solution and stuck to it.

grounding: It shows a girl asked why again and again until she finds she packs after the bell, and she starts packing five minutes before it.
